newsitem.title: CANADA: BA strike challenge for s.east U.S. cargo shippers.
newsitem.headline: BA strike challenge for s.east U.S. cargo shippers.

text.p: Air freight shippers in the southeastern U.S. will have the biggest challenge coping with the 72-hour British Airways Plc cabin crew strike, says a senior airline executive.
"That's where we're going to see the biggest impact, no doubt about it," says Mark Najarian, vice-president sales at American Airlines.
"If you define the southeast as being Washington south, there isn't much flying in that area now."
Shippers are re-routing freight around the labour dispute, but even at New York-JFK, space to London is at a premium.
Najarian said on Tuesday American added an extra flight from JFK to London-Heathrow to today's schedule and the cargo space was snapped up almost immediately.
Southeastern shippers may have better luck trucking to Miami where BA is hoping to operate normally.

British Airways has cancelled flights to all points along the eastern seaboard south of New York and north of Miami. Destinations with no BA service today include Orlando, Atlanta, Charlotte, Baltimore, Washington and Philadelphia.
Besides trucking to other airports, southeastern shippers can look for space on passenger charters, if there happen to be any locally, or try to wait out the strike.

For just-in-time and other time-sensitive shipments, trucking long distances, or waiting out the strike are not realistic options, said Najarian. Nor is re-routing over Paris and Frankfurt a practical option as that will add 1-2 days shipping time for traffic intended for the UK.
The seasonal slowdown after the U.S. July 4 holiday means that there will be some available cargo capacity from some North American gateways.

Delta Airlines, the largest operator from Atlanta to London, said there had been no significant increase in activity attributable to the BA strike, which it said may reflect the large amount of international charters operating from Atlanta.

However, United Airlines, which flies to Heathrow from New York, Chicago and Washington as well as off the West Coast says its flights to London and from are full even without the extra business made available by the strike.
